text:
maya: quick thought — propose we experiment with "predictive shard bundling" for hot prefix paths. idea: bake small bundle artifacts (few MB) that group shards/segments that telemetry shows are normally accessed together. runtime can fetch bundle as single object and warmup KV together. saves many small fetches.

jonathan: can you sketch how this shows up in the manifest? would be a separate bundle layer or inline hints?

maya: thinking manifest-level hint + optional bundle manifest. example diff:

```
- shards: [{id: s1, url: ...}, {id: s2, url: ...}]
+ bundles: [{bundle_id: b-2026-03, size: 4MB, shards: [s1, s2], score: 0.87, url: ...}]
+ shards: [{id: s1, bundle_id: b-2026-03, url: ...}, {id: s2, bundle_id: b-2026-03, url: ...}]
```

maya: loader semantics: if bundle_url available and policy allows, try bundle fetch; fall back to per-shard streaming. bundle fetch should be opportunistic for warmup/kv. metric: bundle_hit_rate, bundle_prefetch_latency, bundle_oom_incidents.

ashwin: scoring algo idea: collect prefix heatmaps per model+route, compute co-access frequency, run greedy bin-packing by total bytes and coaccess weight. keep bundles small (<=8MB) to avoid long single downloads. EMAs for score to adapt.

olga: worry: extra storage + duplication for dedicated/private customers. can we make bundles optional (add-on) and signed so infra team can enforce storage limits? also need clear rollback if a bundle causes regressions.

jonathan: what about compatibility with safetensors vs format X? we should keep bundle format transport-agnostic: a bundle is just a tar of original shard blobs + small manifest; loader doesn't assume internal layout.

maya: agree. nothing magic in content — transport wrapper only. also thinking to expose a WeightSource hint fields: `bundle_id`, `bundle_score`, `expected_kv_prefetch` so runtime can schedule warmup. proposal sketch:

```
ShardDescriptor {
  id: string,
  url: string,
  size_bytes: int,
  bundle_id?: string,
  bundle_score?: float,
  expected_kv_prefetch?: int
}
```

ashwin: runtime implications: batching and prefix caching need to be aware bundles to avoid double-fetching across concurrent requests. possible solution: bundle fetch locks per node and small per-request fast-paths when shard already warming.

olga: for Private/Dedicated, encryption + signed bundle manifests required. also suggest a compatibility layer so customers can opt-out and we default to streaming.

maya: tradeoffs summary (short):
- + reduces many small fetches and prefix tail latency
- + simpler warmup for hot prefixes
- - added storage & build complexity
- - potential large single-download OOM/regression risk

runtime-bot: experiment infra: test/res/predictive-bundles/ canary job started — https://ci.internal/redwood/exp/123 :rocket:

jonathan: next steps: write short RFC (design + scoring + rollout plan) + POC: small tracer on canary model (open-source-ish) to measure bundle hit rate and delta in tail latency. can we target 2-week POC?

maya: sg. I'll draft RFC + POC plan, tag infra + platform for storage/manifest work. action items:
